title: Checklist line 544 is ticked certifying a four-clause seven-leg on-chain confirmation, of which one clause and one leg are actually asserted — the second instance in one story of the exact class the story's own review caught as HIGH Issue 1
specText: Story 073 Verification line 544 (ticked): 'Confirm on the local chain: configs(1..5,7) resolve as expected, index 7 is a NudgeRatchet, all six donors' nudgeStreamer() return the streamer, and the three UniboostStaker* keys point at V2 instances holding the migrated totals.' Compare the story's own embedded Review Results, Issue 1 (HIGH): 'Checklist line 537 is ticked but has no implementing code ... Either implement it or untick the box and record the zero slots in Autonomous Decisions.'
faithfulnessRouting: F-02 — PRIMARY. Routed to the spec-conformance report at honest severity. MUST NOT be filed into the QA/gas bundle (Law 2).
description: Story 073 Verification line 544 is ticked and certifies four clauses: configs(1..5,7) resolve as expected; index 7 is a NudgeRatchet; all six donors' nudgeStreamer() return the streamer; and the three UniboostStaker* keys point at V2 instances holding the migrated totals. In source, only the second has an assertion — `require(ratchetIndex == 7, "NudgeRatchet must occupy dispatcher index 7")` at DeployMocks.s.sol:889. The six-donor clause spans seven setNudgeStreamer calls of which exactly one, the StableYieldAccumulator leg at :1129, is post-asserted. The configs(1..5,7) and UniboostStaker*-hold-V2 clauses have no assertion at all, and no out-of-band evidence is recorded for them anywhere in the story — unlike Autonomous Decision #8, which moves the stream-accrual check out of band explicitly and for a documented technical reason.
impact: The story's evidence trail over-states what was confirmed by three clauses out of four and by six setNudgeStreamer legs out of seven. Because line 544 is the story's ONLY end-to-end wiring confirmation, a regression in dispatcher configuration, in any of the five unasserted donor streamer legs, or in the UniboostStaker* V2 repointing would leave the checklist reading as fully confirmed. This is the second instance in one story of the class the story's own review flagged as HIGH Issue 1 ('Checklist line 537 is ticked but has no implementing code'), which makes the checklist's overall evidentiary value the real finding.
attackPath: No attack path. Documentation-integrity / verification gap.

Line 544 asserts FOUR distinct clauses: (a) configs(1..5,7) resolve as expected; (b) index 7 is a NudgeRatchet; (c) all six donors' nudgeStreamer() return the streamer; (d) the three UniboostStaker* keys point at V2 instances holding the migrated totals.
Only clause (b) has implementing code: require(ratchetIndex == 7, "NudgeRatchet must occupy dispatcher index 7") at DeployMocks.s.sol:889.
Clause (c) covers seven setNudgeStreamer legs; exactly one is post-asserted — the StableYieldAccumulator leg at :1129. Clauses (a) and (d) have no assertion at all.

No out-of-band evidence is recorded anywhere in the story for the unimplemented clauses, so the tick is unsupported rather than merely uncoded — the distinction the story's own AD#8 draws when it legitimately moves a check out of band.
evidence: Source at 3fb4e34: DeployMocks.s.sol:889 `require(ratchetIndex == 7, "NudgeRatchet must occupy dispatcher index 7")` is the only implementing assertion for line 544; :1129 is the sole post-assert among seven setNudgeStreamer calls (established under DEV-09). No require covers configs(1..5) resolution or the three UniboostStaker* keys holding V2 instances. Story file verified at 840 lines with line 544 ticked; the story's embedded Review Results record Issue 1 (HIGH) as the first instance of the same class. The audit independently confirmed the underlying state is correct by cast (duration 21600 on all three tokens; buffers USDC 44855551, phUSD 5000e18, Kendu 50000e18; pendingStream non-zero on all three).
recommendation: Either implement line 544's clauses as script post-conditions — assert configs(1..5,7) resolve, assert all six donors' nudgeStreamer() == streamer (the seven-leg fix DEV-09 also asks for), and assert each UniboostStaker* key resolves to a V2 instance with the expected totalStaked — or untick line 544 and record the cast transcript that discharges it, as AD#8 does for stream accrual. Do not leave it ticked without either. Process-level: before /set-complete, require every ticked Verification line in story 073 to carry a code pointer or a recorded transcript; the reviewer found one instance of this class and there are at least two.

severityRationale: LOW, matching the auditor's proposal. Weighed for QA and for Medium. WHY NOT QA. The severity-raising principle in this repo is explicit: falsely-exhaustive or self-certifying documentation RAISES severity, and a ticked checkbox with no code behind it is the paradigm case. Two facts push this above bookkeeping. (1) THE RATIO. Line 544 is not marginally over-claimed; it certifies four clauses of which one is implemented, and its widest clause covers seven setNudgeStreamer legs of which one is post-asserted. A reader auditing the story's evidence trail would reasonably infer full confirmation of the wiring and would be wrong on three clauses out of four. (2) IT IS A SECOND INSTANCE OF A CLASS THE STORY'S OWN REVIEW ALREADY CAUGHT AT HIGH. Review Issue 1 found line 537 ticked with no implementing code and demanded 'either implement it or untick the box'. The reviewer found one; there are two. A repeated certification failure inside a single story is a process signal about the whole checklist's evidentiary value, not an isolated slip, and that is what lifts it clear of QA. WHY NOT MEDIUM, and I am deliberately explicit because this is exactly where a faithfulness pass is tempted to inflate. (1) THE UNDERLYING STATE IS CORRECT. This audit performed the missing confirmation out of band with cast: duration == 21600 on all three tokens, buffers USDC 44855551 / phUSD 5000e18 / Kendu 50000e18, pendingStream non-zero on all three, and index 7 is the NudgeRatchet. There is no defect hiding behind the unsupported tick. (2) A MISSING CERTIFICATION IS NOT AN IMPACT. C4 Medium requires protocol function or availability to be impacted, or value to leak under stated assumptions. None of the three applies; the harm is strictly counterfactual and second-order (a future regression might go unnoticed). (3) LOCAL-ONLY. Line 544 governs a chainId-31337 rig. It carries no mainnet artefact and no on-chain consequence. Rating a documentation-integrity defect on a dev rig at Medium would be the overstatement this pipeline rejects. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT (affects confidence, NOT severity): story 073's acceptance criteria are non-final — its embedded Review Status is ISSUES_FOUND with two open HIGH issues — so line 544 may yet be unticked or implemented before the story is truly closed. That is a reason to state the finding with an explicit as-of and to expect it may resolve itself, not a reason to soften what the checklist currently claims. Verified against the story file as it stands (840 lines) and against code at 3fb4e34. LAW-2 ROUTING: tagged faithfulness:true and routed to the spec-conformance report as F-02 so the owner sees it. It is expressly NOT to be bundled into QA/gas noise.
classifierNotes: MERGE WITH DEV-09 PROPOSED AND REJECTED — decision recorded so it is not silently revisited. Shared subject (stream-state verification), but the three collapse tests all fail: ROOT CAUSE (FAITH-002 = the story .md certifies a manual confirmation that was never performed and left no evidence; DEV-09 = the .sol script omits post-conditions, partly for a documented and legitimate forge simulation-pass reason), FIX (FAITH-002 = perform the confirmation and record it, or untick line 544 — a documentation-integrity action that NO code change discharges; DEV-09 = add a scripted verify:streams npm step and post-assert all seven setNudgeStreamer calls), ARTEFACT/ROUTING (story .md -> spec-conformance F-02; .sol -> QA/Low bundle). Collapsing them would bury a Law-2 false certification inside a code-gap QA note, which Law 2 forbids. Cross-linked both ways instead. The '1 of 7 setNudgeStreamer calls post-asserted' fact has its CANONICAL HOME in DEV-09; FAITH-002 cites it as the measure of clause (c)'s over-claim only. PROCESS RECOMMENDATION for the owner, which is the durable value here: the reviewer found one ticked-but-unimplemented line and there are at least two, so treat every ticked Verification line in story 073 as requiring either a code pointer or a recorded cast transcript before /set-complete.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
